Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). 1	# Plan: M1 + M4 — Real data foundation + eval baseline
2	
3	**Status: pending approval**
4	**Created:** 2026-08-14 · **Scope source:** `.omc/plans/cybernaut-mini-rebuild.md` (M1, M4) as amended by `.omc/wiki/cybernaut-mini-scope-decisions-2026-07-28.md` Amendment 2026-08-08 (#6, #7, #8)
5	
6	## Requirements summary
7	
8	- Replace all synthetic data with real data per Amendment #8: **CC-News spine** (`stanford-oval/ccnews`) + **MIRACL eval substrate** (`miracl/miracl-corpus` + MIRACL qrels). English first; Japanese arrives with M13. The current prod source `NOSIBLE/prediction` (conf/prod/catalog.yml:12) is ruled out as a corpus by Amendment #6 and gets replaced.
9	- First real build: **~200k documents / 256 shards** (user chose the ~200-shard scale; 256 keeps the existing power-of-two prod convention — ~780 docs/shard, between prod's current 390 and the scope target's 1,000).
10	- Record per-mode baselines (lexical / dense / hybrid / agent): Recall@5/10, MRR@10, nDCG@10, plus a new **shard_recall@N**.
11	- M1 done-when (roadmap): "real corpus builds; no fabricated record remains anywhere."
12	- Amendment #7 rule: MIRACL-qrels metrics and (future) generated per-shard evals are **never averaged, merged, or reported as one figure**.
13	
14	## Phase 0 — land the WIP first
15	
16	~2,900 uncommitted insertions across 21 files. M1 deletes/renames files the WIP also touches (`tests/conftest.py`, `Makefile`, conf files), so land it first in atomic commits:
17	
18	1. query pipeline s1–s8 + stage tests
19	2. storage.py / shard_artifacts.py / accel.py + their tests
20	3. config / models / embeddings / retrieval / routing refactor
21	4. scripts + devcontainer + docs
22	
23	## Phase 1 — M1: real data foundation
24	
25	1. **Discovery spike (no code).** Resolve `stanford-oval/ccnews` schema (column names, language field, configs/splits, size) and `miracl/miracl-corpus` + MIRACL topics/qrels layout for `en` dev. Pin both SHAs via `HfApi().dataset_info(...).sha`. Output: exact column lists + SHAs, pasted into conf in step 6.
26	2. **Streaming loader.** `HuggingFaceDataset.load` (src/cybernaut_mini/datasets.py:188–225) materialises the full split before the `split[:max_rows]` slice — unusable at CC-News scale. Add `streaming: bool = False` using `load_dataset(..., streaming=True)` + `itertools.islice(max_rows)`; keep the missing-column guard via first-row keys. Unit tests with a mocked `datasets` module; non-streaming behaviour byte-identical.
27	3. **Multi-source ingest.** `corpus_ingest` is single-source (snapshot → normalize → select, src/cybernaut_mini/pipelines/corpus_ingest/nodes.py). Add a second source branch (ccnews + miracl), per-source `CorpusSourceConfig` (src/cybernaut_mini/corpus.py:61) with `id_prefix` `ccn` / `mir` to prevent id collisions, and a `merge_documents` node before `select_documents`. Nodes stay pure; sources come from the catalog.
28	4. **MIRACL qrels → Judgment.** New loader mapping MIRACL `en` dev topics + qrels onto `Judgment {query_id, question, relevant_document_ids: dict[str,int]}` (src/cybernaut_mini/models.py:255). Prod catalog override for `judgments` → `data/03_primary/miracl_en_dev_judgments.jsonl`.

# Plan: M1 + M4 — Real data foundation + eval baseline

**Status: pending approval**
**Created:** 2026-08-14 · **Scope source:** `.omc/plans/cybernaut-mini-rebuild.md` (M1, M4) as amended by `.omc/wiki/cybernaut-mini-scope-decisions-2026-07-28.md` Amendment 2026-08-08 (#6, #7, #8)

## Requirements summary

- Replace all synthetic data with real data per Amendment #8: **CC-News spine** (`stanford-oval/ccnews`) + **MIRACL eval substrate** (`miracl/miracl-corpus` + MIRACL qrels). English first; Japanese arrives with M13. The current prod source `NOSIBLE/prediction` (conf/prod/catalog.yml:12) is ruled out as a corpus by Amendment #6 and gets replaced.
- First real build: **~200k documents / 256 shards** (user chose the ~200-shard scale; 256 keeps the existing power-of-two prod convention — ~780 docs/shard, between prod's current 390 and the scope target's 1,000).
- Record per-mode baselines (lexical / dense / hybrid / agent): Recall@5/10, MRR@10, nDCG@10, plus a new **shard_recall@N**.
- M1 done-when (roadmap): "real corpus builds; no fabricated record remains anywhere."
- Amendment #7 rule: MIRACL-qrels metrics and (future) generated per-shard evals are **never averaged, merged, or reported as one figure**.

## Phase 0 — land the WIP first

~2,900 uncommitted insertions across 21 files. M1 deletes/renames files the WIP also touches (`tests/conftest.py`, `Makefile`, conf files), so land it first in atomic commits:

1. query pipeline s1–s8 + stage tests
2. storage.py / shard_artifacts.py / accel.py + their tests
3. config / models / embeddings / retrieval / routing refactor
4. scripts + devcontainer + docs

## Phase 1 — M1: real data foundation

1. **Discovery spike (no code).** Resolve `stanford-oval/ccnews` schema (column names, language field, configs/splits, size) and `miracl/miracl-corpus` + MIRACL topics/qrels layout for `en` dev. Pin both SHAs via `HfApi().dataset_info(...).sha`. Output: exact column lists + SHAs, pasted into conf in step 6.
2. **Streaming loader.** `HuggingFaceDataset.load` (src/cybernaut_mini/datasets.py:188–225) materialises the full split before the `split[:max_rows]` slice — unusable at CC-News scale. Add `streaming: bool = False` using `load_dataset(..., streaming=True)` + `itertools.islice(max_rows)`; keep the missing-column guard via first-row keys. Unit tests with a mocked `datasets` module; non-streaming behaviour byte-identical.
3. **Multi-source ingest.** `corpus_ingest` is single-source (snapshot → normalize → select, src/cybernaut_mini/pipelines/corpus_ingest/nodes.py). Add a second source branch (ccnews + miracl), per-source `CorpusSourceConfig` (src/cybernaut_mini/corpus.py:61) with `id_prefix` `ccn` / `mir` to prevent id collisions, and a `merge_documents` node before `select_documents`. Nodes stay pure; sources come from the catalog.
4. **MIRACL qrels → Judgment.** New loader mapping MIRACL `en` dev topics + qrels onto `Judgment {query_id, question, relevant_document_ids: dict[str,int]}` (src/cybernaut_mini/models.py:255). Prod catalog override for `judgments` → `data/03_primary/miracl_en_dev_judgments.jsonl`.
5. **Corpus composition (fidelity rule).** Every doc referenced by MIRACL-en dev qrels MUST be in the corpus (else recall is artificially capped): stream-filter the MIRACL corpus by the qrels docid set (small, ~thousands), snapshot to `data/01_raw/` (raw layer = never re-download, nodes.py:38 principle). Fill the remaining budget to 200k with CC-News-en via `max_rows` on the ccnews branch.
6. **Prod conf rewrite.** conf/prod/catalog.yml: replace the `NOSIBLE/prediction` source with the two pinned sources; artifact paths prefixed `ccnews_miracl_`. conf/prod/parameters.yml: per-source `corpus` field_maps, `corpus_selection.languages: [en]`, `index.n_shards: 256`.
7. **Fixture slice replaces `data/sample/`.** Commit a small REAL slice: all docs for ~25 MIRACL dev queries (incl. every qrels positive) + ~200 CC-News docs, with real qrels, to `data/01_raw/fixtures/`. Update `configs/tiny.yaml`, Makefile `build-sample`/`search-sample`/`eval-sample` → `*-fixture` (Makefile:17–32), `tests/conftest.py`, and every test reading `data/sample`.
8. **Licensing.** `data/ATTRIBUTION.md` + `data/LICENSE-DATA`: CC-News (per-article publisher copyright, Common Crawl ToU, cite stanford-oval/ccnews + SHA), MIRACL (Apache-2.0 + SHA).
9. **Deletions.** `data/sample/*`, `scripts/generate_sample_corpus.py`; then `rg "data/sample|generate_sample_corpus"` must be clean. M1 done-when satisfied.

## Phase 2 — M4: eval baseline

1. **`shard_recall@N`** in src/cybernaut_mini/evals.py (+ EvalMetrics fields, evals.py:107) and the evaluation nodes (src/cybernaut_mini/pipelines/evaluation/nodes.py:49): fraction of qrels-positive docs whose home shard is among the N shards the router selected (N = configured beam width). Per-mode breakdown.
2. **Baseline run.** `scripts/with-accel.sh uv run kedro run --env prod --pipeline production` (200k docs, e5-small on MPS), then `--pipeline evaluation`. Record wall-clock + peak RSS. Dry-run first at `max_rows≈20k` to calibrate build time before committing to the full run.
3. **Baseline doc.** `docs/baselines/ccnews-miracl-200k.md`: per-mode table (4 modes × 5 metrics), corpus SHAs, embedder revision (conf/prod/parameters.yml:9), shard count, build time. Wiki page updated. MIRACL metrics labelled as benchmark metrics — never merged with per-shard generated evals (Amendment #7).
4. **Sanity gates (recording, not tuning).** hybrid must not underperform BOTH lexical and dense; shard_recall@N must beat a random-N-shards baseline. On failure: file the issue and stop — tuning belongs to M5–M11.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `rg -l "data/sample|generate_sample_corpus"` returns no source/test/conf hits.
2. `kedro run --env prod --pipeline production` completes; index at 256 shards; document count in [190k, 200k].
3. Every docid in `miracl_en_dev_judgments.jsonl` exists in the built index (asserted in `validate_judgments`).
4. `kedro run --env prod --pipeline evaluation` writes `data/08_reporting/eval_report.json` with 4 modes × 5 metrics including shard_recall@N; no mode is all-zero/NaN.
5. `make test` passes fully offline using the committed real fixture slice.
6. `data/ATTRIBUTION.md` + `data/LICENSE-DATA` exist, naming both datasets with pinned SHAs.
7. Streaming loader unit-tested; loading 100 CC-News rows takes < 60 s and does not download full shards (HF cache size checked).
8. `docs/baselines/ccnews-miracl-200k.md` committed with non-placeholder numbers.

## Risks & mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| CC-News full download is tens of GB | Streaming loader (Phase 1.2) is a hard prerequisite; verify islice stops network reads (acceptance 7) |
| MIRACL corpus is ~32M passages | Only stream-filter by the small qrels docid set once; snapshot to 01_raw so it never re-downloads |
| ccnews schema differs from assumptions | Discovery spike (Phase 1.1) before any code |
| Fixture-slice licensing (CC-News articles are publisher-copyrighted) | Keep slice < 250 CC-News docs, per-source attribution, educational use; fallback: MIRACL-only fixture (Apache-2.0) |
| 200k × e5-small build time on M-series unknown | 20k calibration run first; model2vec fast-real path documented as fallback |
| Real embeddings break determinism | Pinned SHAs, id-sorted selection (corpus_ingest/nodes.py:97), floats rounded in report |

## Verification steps

1. `make test` offline — green (933+ tests).
2. Streaming spike: 100 ccnews rows < 60 s, bounded HF cache growth.
3. Post-build: acceptance criteria 2–4.
4. `scripts/devcontainer_doctor.sh` still green (its catalog check catches renames).
5. `git log --oneline` shows Phase 0 landed as ≥4 atomic commits before any M1 commit.

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## huggingface
You have tools for using the Hugging Face Hub. Hugging Face tools are being used by authenticated user 'neelan'
hf:// URIs can be converted to browser URLs by replacing hf://buckets/OWNER/NAME/PATH with https://huggingface.co/buckets/OWNER/NAME/resolve/PATH; for models, datasets, and spaces, use https://huggingface.co[/datasets|/spaces]/OWNER/NAME/resolve/main/PATH. URL-encode each path segment. arXiv paper id's are often used as references between datasets, models and papers. There are over 100 tags in use, common tags include 'Text Generation', 'Transformers', 'Image Classification' and so on.

## numerai
IMPORTANT INSTRUCTIONS FOR USING THE NUMERAI MCP SERVER:

This server provides several tools for interacting with the Numerai Tournament API.
All functionality is accessed by calling these tools directly — they are already
available in your tool catalog via tools/list. Do NOT call list_mcp_resources or
list_mcp_resource_templates to discover functionality. The tools are already loaded.

When a user asks what you can do with Numerai, or asks about Numerai capabilities,
IMMEDIATELY all tools/list to list these tools and offer to call them. Do not search
for resources first.

TERMINOLOGY:
- "Models" are prediction algorithms submitted by participants
- "Accounts" are people/entities who own models — one account can have many models
- Tournament 8 = "Classic", 11 = "Signals", 12 = "CryptoSignals"

KEY METRICS:
- mmcRep = meta-model contribution reputation (main performance score)
- fncV3Rep = feature-neutral correlation v3 reputation
- return13Weeks = 13-week return on staked NMR
- nmrStaked = NMR cryptocurrency staked on the model
- latestReps = nested object with current reputation scores (corr, mmc, fnc)
- latestRanks = nested object with current rankings
- latestReturns = nested object with return data (oneDay, threeMonths, oneYear)

AUTH: Users pass API tokens via the Authorization header or the apiToken parameter.

per shard at load time. At the project's target scale — 1,000,000 documents over
1,000 shards, the ratio the post discloses — that is roughly 20 GB of heap on a

the three primitives that replace eager loading: random access into a JSONL file
by record id, memory-mapped embeddings, and a bounded cache for the per-shard

2	
3	A shard in Cybernaut-1 is not just a list of document ids. The post enumerates what
4	lives inside one, and three of those entries are routing *filters* rather than
5	rankers: a bloom filter of important phrases, a trained Zstandard compression
6	dictionary, and the shard's vocabulary. This module builds all three as pure
7	functions over already-extracted text, and defines the JSON serialisation contract
8	that lets a shard manifest carry them.

11	value objects out, so they can be exercised at a scale (1,000 shards) where nothing

17	the bloom filter: rBloom hashes with :func:`hash` by default, and CPython salts

"""The three per-shard routing artifacts the blog lists but this repo did not have.

A shard in Cybernaut-1 is not just a list of document ids. The post enumerates what
lives inside one, and three of those entries are routing *filters* rather than
rankers: a bloom filter of important phrases, a trained Zstandard compression
dictionary, and the shard's vocabulary. This module builds all three as pure
functions over already-extracted text, and defines the JSON serialisation contract
that lets a shard manifest carry them.

Nothing here loads or writes an index; the builders take text in and return small
value objects out, so they can be exercised at a scale (1,000 shards) where nothing
that materialises a corpus can be.

Determinism
-----------
Every artifact is byte-identical across processes for the same input. The trap is
the bloom filter: rBloom hashes with :func:`hash` by default, and CPython salts
:func:`hash` for ``str`` and ``bytes`` with ``PYTHONHASHSEED``, so a filter built in
one process is meaningless in the next. rBloom guards its own ``save_bytes`` against
the *built-in* hash, but a caller-supplied ``lambda o: hash(o)`` slips straight
through the guard and silently produces a different bit pattern per process. This
module therefore never lets a hash function be chosen: it pins BLAKE2b-128
(:func:`stable_hash`), records that choice in the payload, and refuses to reload a
payload written under a different one.

Zstandard is deterministic on its own terms once training is single-threaded: with
``threads=0`` the COVER parameter search is a fixed computation over the samples, and
a ``dict_id`` of 0 makes zstd derive the id from the dictionary content rather than
generating a random one.

feat(storage): add disk-backed storage, shard artifacts, and accel survey

a bounded shard cache — the three primitives that replace eager heap loading
at the million-doc scale described in the blog post.

shard_artifacts.py: builds the three per-shard routing artifacts the blog

dictionary, shard vocabulary). Pure functions over text so they run at 1,000-
shard scale without materialising a corpus.

accel.py: hardware survey — resolve_device (torch MPS/CUDA/CPU), tuning_env
(thread counts), describe (human-readable report), device_fingerprint. Named
the BLAS/torch/native/pure-Python layers so the survey output shows exactly
where performance lives and where it does not.

scripts/with-accel.sh: small wrapper that exports the tuning env vars before
invoking a build, so e.g. kedro runs pick up the MPS device automatically.

Tests cover storage (sidecar index, mmap reads, LRU eviction), shard
artifacts (bloom fpr, zstd round-trip, vocab extraction), accel (device
resolution, env var generation), and an index-scale smoke test at 1k shards.
EOF
)"

_TITLE_MAX_CHARS = 120

_SENTENCE_END = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+")
_WHITESPACE = re.compile(r"\s+")


class CorpusSourceConfig(BaseModel):
    """How to turn raw source rows into :class:`Document` records."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    #: Source column -> Document field. Values must name real Document fields.
    field_map: dict[str, str] = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: {
            "text": "text",
            "url": "url",
        }
    )
    #: Source columns copied verbatim into ``Document.metadata``.
    metadata_fields: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    #: Applied when the source carries no per-row language column.
    default_language: str | None = "en"
    #: Prefix for generated ids, so documents from different sources cannot collide.
    id_prefix: str = "doc"
    #: Drop documents whose body is shorter than this (boilerplate, nav text).
    min_text_chars: int = Field(default=32, ge=0)


class CorpusNormalizeError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a source cannot be mapped onto the Document schema at all."""


def _clean(value: Any) -> str:
    """Collapse whitespace in a source value; non-strings become empty."""
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return ""
    return _WHITESPACE.sub(" ", value).strip()


def derive_title(text: str) -> str:
    """Use the first sentence as the title, truncated on a word boundary.

    These corpora ship passages without titles, but the shard manifest, the shard
    summary, and the ``title\\ntext`` embedding input all assume one exists.
    """
    first = _SENTENCE_END.split(text, maxsplit=1)[0].strip()
    if not first:
        first = text.strip()
    if len(first) <= _TITLE_MAX_CHARS:
        return first
    clipped = first[:_TITLE_MAX_CHARS].rsplit(" ", 1)[0].strip()
    # A single token longer than the cap leaves nothing after rsplit; hard-cut it.
    return clipped or first[:_TITLE_MAX_CHARS]


def make_document_id(prefix: str, natural_key: str) -> str:
    """Stable id from the row's natural key, so ids survive a re-run."""
    digest = hashlib.blake2b(natural_key.encode("utf-8"), digest_size=8).hexdigest()
    return f"{prefix}-{digest}"


def normalize_rows(
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]],
    config: CorpusSourceConfig,
) -> list[Document]:
    """Map raw source rows onto validated, deduplicated :class:`Document` records.

    Rows that are unusable — no body text, or shorter than ``min_text_chars`` — are
    skipped rather than raised on: a 100k-row public corpus is expected to contain
    some junk, and one bad row must not fail a production build. Duplicate natural
    keys collapse to their first occurrence. Ordering is by document id so the
    result is independent of the source's row order.

    Raises :class:`CorpusNormalizeError` only for problems that make the *whole*
    source unusable, such as a ``field_map`` that never resolves a text column.
    """
    if not rows:
        return []

    text_sources = [src for src, dest in config.field_map.items() if dest == "text"]

field_map:

---

**SHA (pinned 2026-08-14):** `5be20db9509754dadad47689368639fcec739c00`  
**Gated:** No  
**Format:** TSV files (no header row), TREC-style

| File | Rows |
|---|---|
| `miracl-v1.0-en/topics/topics.miracl-v1.0-en-dev.tsv` | 799 queries |
| `miracl-v1.0-en/qrels/qrels.miracl-v1.0-en-dev.tsv` | 8,350 qrel rows |

**Topics:** `{query_id}\t{question}` — e.g. `0\tIs Creole a pidgin of French?`

**Qrels (TREC):** `{query_id}\tQ0\t{docid}\t{grade}`

### Judgment field map

```python
Judgment(
    query_id=str(query_id),
    question=question,
    relevant_document_ids={
        make_document_id("mir", docid): int(grade)
        for (query_id, _, docid, grade) in qrel_rows
        if query_id == this_query_id
    }
)
```

---

## 4. Gating / authentication

Neither dataset requires `HF_TOKEN`. The env var is available but not needed for
these two sources. Note for future: MIRACL train qrels (`qrels.miracl-v1.0-en-train.tsv`)
also exists if we want more eval queries later.

---

## 5. Corpus fidelity requirement

7,921 unique docids are referenced by the 799 en-dev queries. **All 7,921 must be
in the built corpus** (plan requirement: stream-filter MIRACL corpus by the qrels
docid set, snapshot to `data/01_raw/`, then fill remainder to 200k with CC-News).
The qrels docid set is small enough to hold in memory as a Python `set`.

# M1.1 Discovery Spike — CC-News + MIRACL schemas and SHAs

**Date:** 2026-08-14  **Author:** worker-1

## 1. CC-News (`stanford-oval/ccnews`)

**SHA:** `d733e654c9a506df519e1a166a86c118c7657ce4` · **Gated:** No · **Config/split:** `default/train` · **Size:** 100M–1B rows (multilingual, 479 parquet shards, 2016+)  
**Loading note:** Deprecated loading script — use `streaming=True` without `trust_remote_code`.

### Columns

| Column | Type | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| `plain_text` | string | `Document.text` |
| `requested_url` | string | `Document.url` (also natural key → stable id) |
| `title` | string | `Document.title` |
| `language` | string | `Document.language` — ISO codes e.g. `"en"`, `"fr"` |
| `published_date` | string | `Document.published_at` — ISO date e.g. `"2016-10-18"` |
| `language_score` | float64 | metadata |
| `publisher` / `sitename` / `author` | string | metadata |
| `tags` / `categories` / `image_url` / `responded_url` / `warc_path` / `crawl_date` | string | discard |

### Recommended `CorpusSourceConfig`

```yaml
field_map:
  plain_text: text
  requested_url: url
  title: title
  language: language
  published_date: published_at
metadata_fields: [publisher, sitename, author]
id_prefix: ccn
default_language: en
```

**Streaming filter:** `language == "en"` before `islice(max_rows)` so the cap
applies to English rows only, not the full multilingual stream.

---

## 2. MIRACL corpus (`miracl/miracl-corpus`)

**SHA:** `d921ec7e349ce0d28daf30b2da9da5ee698bef0d` · **Gated:** No  
**Format:** JSONL.gz — loading script deprecated; use `hf_hub_download` per shard or `HfFileSystem`.  
**Path pattern:** `miracl-corpus-v1.0-en/docs-{N}.jsonl.gz`

### Columns

| Column | Type | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| `docid` | string | `Document.url` (natural key → `mir-blake2b(docid)`) |
| `title` | string | `Document.title` |
| `text` | string | `Document.text` |

**docid format:** `{wikipedia_page_id}#{passage_index}` e.g. `"12#0"`

### Recommended `CorpusSourceConfig`

```yaml
field_map:
  text: text
  title: title
  docid: url       # drives stable id: mir-blake2b(docid)
metadata_fields: [docid]   # preserve original for qrel→doc lookup debugging
id_prefix: mir
default_language: en
```

**Design note for Task #5 (Judgment loader):** `relevant_document_ids` keys must
be `make_document_id("mir", qrel_docid)` so they match the built `Document.id`.
The loader should call `corpus.make_document_id("mir", docid)` for each qrel row.

---

## 3. MIRACL topics + qrels (`miracl/miracl`)

**SHA (pinned 2026-08-14):** `5be20db9509754dadad47689368639fcec739c00`  
**Gated:** No  
**Format:** TSV files (no header row), TREC-style

### en dev counts

| File | Rows |
|---|---|
| `miracl-v1.0-en/topics/topics.miracl-v1.0-en-dev.tsv` | 799 queries |
| `miracl-v1.0-en/qrels/qrels.miracl-v1.0-en-dev.tsv` | 8,350 qrel rows |
| Unique docids in qrels | 7,921 |

### TSV formats

**Topics:** `{query_id}\t{question}` — e.g. `0\tIs Creole a pidgin of French?`

**Qrels (TREC):** `{query_id}\tQ0\t{docid}\t{grade}`  
Grade values: `0` (not relevant), `1` (relevant)

### Judgment field map

```python
Judgment(
    query_id=str(query_id),
    question=question,
    relevant_document_ids={
        make_document_id("mir", docid): int(grade)
        for (query_id, _, docid, grade) in qrel_rows
        if query_id == this_query_id
    }
)
```

---

## 4. Notes

- **Gating:** Neither dataset requires `HF_TOKEN`.
- **Fidelity:** 7,921 unique docids across 799 en-dev queries must all be in the
  built corpus. Stream-filter MIRACL corpus by the qrels docid set (fits in memory
  as a Python `set`), snapshot to `data/01_raw/`, fill remainder to 200k with CC-News.
- **MIRACL train split** (`qrels.miracl-v1.0-en-train.tsv`) exists for future use.

# Production catalog overrides: `kedro run --env prod --pipeline production`.
#
# Only the acquisition source changes. Every downstream entry is inherited from
# conf/base/catalog.yml unchanged, which is the point of routing data through the
# catalog: the pipeline code that builds a 100k-document shard is the same code
# that builds the 66-document sample.
#
# Requires the `hf` extra:  uv sync --extra hf --extra st
# Private/gated repos additionally need HF_TOKEN in the environment.

raw_corpus_source:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.HuggingFaceDataset
  repo_id: NOSIBLE/prediction
  # REQUIRED: an immutable commit SHA or tag. Branch names and this placeholder
  # are both rejected at load time, so an unpinned corpus cannot reach a build.
  # Resolved 2026-08-14 from:
  #   uv run python -c "from huggingface_hub import HfApi; \
  #     print(HfApi().dataset_info('NOSIBLE/prediction').sha)"
  revision: eefc2260041afc60bb8f8e343cf43a20e7828a4a
  split: train
  columns: [text, label, netloc, url]
  # Uncapped: the full 100,000 rows (26.9 MB parquet, 71.4 MB in Arrow). Set
  # max_rows to dial in a faster build; the cap is a prefix, not a sample, so a
  # capped run is not a statistically valid preview of the full one.

# Keep production artifacts out of the sample paths so a prod run can never
# overwrite the committed sample index.
raw_corpus:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/01_raw/prediction_snapshot.jsonl

normalized_documents:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/02_intermediate/prediction_documents.jsonl

documents:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:input_path,data/03_primary/prediction_corpus.jsonl}

shard_index:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.ShardIndexDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:index_path,artifacts/prediction}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# MIRACL en-dev judgment pipeline (task #5 / M1.4)                   #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Run standalone: kedro run --env prod --pipeline judgment_ingest
# Or as part of production (documents must exist first for validation).

miracl_en_dev_source:
  # load_dataset("miracl/miracl") is blocked by a deprecated loading script
  # (miracl.py). MiraclTsvDataset reads the underlying TSV files directly via
  # HfFileSystem and assembles them into the same structured row format.
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.MiraclTsvDataset
  repo_id: miracl/miracl
  # SHA pinned 2026-08-14 from:
  #   uv run python -c "from huggingface_hub import HfApi; \
  #     print(HfApi().dataset_info('miracl/miracl').sha)"
  revision: 5be20db9509754dadad47689368639fcec739c00
  language: en
  split: dev

# Intermediate: unvalidated judgments before the corpus cross-check.
miracl_judgments_unvalidated:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/02_intermediate/miracl_en_dev_judgments_unvalidated.jsonl

# Final validated judgments consumed by the evaluation pipeline.
judgments:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/03_primary/miracl_en_dev_judgments.jsonl

content.content:
137	class HuggingFaceDataset(AbstractDataset[None, list[dict[str, Any]]]):
138	    """Read-only corpus source backed by a Hugging Face Hub dataset repo.
139	
140	    ``revision`` is **required and must be a commit SHA or tag**, never a branch
141	    name: a production shard is only reproducible if the corpus it was built from
142	    is pinned. ``main`` is rejected outright.
143	
144	    Set ``streaming=True`` for large datasets (CC-News is hundreds of GB in full):
145	    the loader opens an :class:`~datasets.IterableDataset` over Arrow shards and
146	    uses :func:`itertools.islice` so only ``max_rows`` rows are downloaded rather
147	    than materialising a whole shard boundary.
148	
149	    ``filter_equals`` pre-filters rows in streaming mode **before** the
150	    ``max_rows`` cap is applied, so the cap counts only rows that pass the
151	    filter. Use this to restrict a multilingual corpus to a single language
152	    without downloading rows that will be dropped — e.g. for CC-News:
153	    ``filter_equals: {language: en}``.
154	
155	    Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — CC-News as a
156	        corpus source; 200k-document builds are the target scale (Phase 1.2).
157	
158	    Assumptions:
159	        - ``IterableDataset.features`` is populated from the dataset's Arrow
160	          schema metadata without iterating rows, so the missing-column check
161	          can inspect it before consuming any data. When ``features`` is

class HuggingFaceDataset(AbstractDataset[None, list[dict[str, Any]]]):
    """Read-only corpus source backed by a Hugging Face Hub dataset repo.

    ``revision`` is **required and must be a commit SHA or tag**, never a branch
    name: a production shard is only reproducible if the corpus it was built from
    is pinned. ``main`` is rejected outright.

    Set ``streaming=True`` for large datasets (CC-News is hundreds of GB in full):
    the loader opens an :class:`~datasets.IterableDataset` over Arrow shards and
    uses :func:`itertools.islice` so only ``max_rows`` rows are downloaded rather
    than materialising a whole shard boundary.

    ``filter_equals`` pre-filters rows in streaming mode **before** the
    ``max_rows`` cap is applied, so the cap counts only rows that pass the
    filter. Use this to restrict a multilingual corpus to a single language
    without downloading rows that will be dropped — e.g. for CC-News:
    ``filter_equals: {language: en}``.

    Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — CC-News as a
        corpus source; 200k-document builds are the target scale (Phase 1.2).

    Assumptions:
        - ``IterableDataset.features`` is populated from the dataset's Arrow
          schema metadata without iterating rows, so the missing-column check
          can inspect it before consuming any data. When ``features`` is
          ``None`` (a dynamically typed transform was chained upstream), the
          check falls back to the first row's keys and re-inserts that row so
          nothing is lost.
        - ``filter_equals`` is applied in streaming mode only. The eager path
          materialises the whole split first; for large multilingual corpora
          ``streaming=True`` is therefore mandatory.

    Alternatives rejected:
        - ``IterableDataset.select_columns`` for projection in streaming mode.
          Supported since ``datasets>=2.4`` but adds another lazy wrapper; a
          per-row dict comprehension is simpler and independent of the exact
          ``datasets`` API version.
        - Filtering in ``select_documents`` rather than here: would download
          millions of non-English CC-News rows into the raw snapshot, wasting
          disk and network just to drop them.

    Requires the ``hf`` extra (``uv sync --extra hf``). The import is deferred to
    :meth:`load` so the core package — and the whole offline test suite — never
    depends on it.
    """

    #: Refs that move over time and so cannot pin a reproducible build.
    _MUTABLE_REFS = frozenset({"main", "master", "head", "refs/heads/main"})

    #: Shipped in conf/prod as a deliberate tripwire — a real SHA must replace it.
    _PLACEHOLDER_REF = "replace_with_commit_sha"

    def __init__(
        self,
        repo_id: str,
        revision: str,
        split: str = "train",
        config: str | None = None,
        columns: list[str] | None = None,
        max_rows: int | None = None,
        token_env: str = "HF_TOKEN",
        streaming: bool = False,
        filter_equals: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        normalized_ref = (revision or "").strip().lower()
        if normalized_ref == self._PLACEHOLDER_REF:
            msg = (
                f"HuggingFaceDataset({repo_id!r}): revision is still the placeholder. "
                f"Resolve the real SHA and paste it into conf/prod/catalog.yml:\n"
                f"  uv run python -c \"from huggingface_hub import HfApi; "
                f"print(HfApi().dataset_info('{repo_id}').sha)\""
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg)
        if not normalized_ref or normalized_ref in self._MUTABLE_REFS:
            msg = (
                f"HuggingFaceDataset({repo_id!r}): revision must pin an immutable "
                f"commit SHA or tag, got {revision!r}. A moving ref makes the built "
                f"index unreproducible."
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg)
        self._repo_id = repo_id
        self._revision = revision
        self._split = split
        self._config = config
        self._columns = columns
        self._max_rows = max_rows
        self._token_env = token_env
        self._streaming = streaming
        self._filter_equals = filter_equals

    def load(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        try:
            # The Hugging Face `datasets` package, not this module: Python 3 has no
            # implicit relative imports, so the absolute name wins despite the clash.
            from datasets import load_dataset
        except ImportError as exc:
            msg = (
                "HuggingFaceDataset needs the 'hf' extra; install it with "
                "`uv sync --extra hf`"
            )

class HfFileDataset(AbstractDataset[None, list[dict[str, Any]]]):
    """Read-only corpus source backed by JSONL.gz files on the Hugging Face Hub.

    For datasets whose ``load_dataset`` loading script is deprecated (e.g.
    ``miracl/miracl-corpus``), individual shard files are accessed directly via
    :class:`huggingface_hub.HfFileSystem` rather than the ``datasets`` library.
    The caller supplies a glob pattern relative to the repo root; matching shards
    are read in alphabetical order so the result is deterministic.

    Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — MIRACL corpus
        as the fidelity substrate for eval; every docid in the qrels must land in
        the built index. Local copy: ``docs/blog-archive/the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md``.

    Assumptions:
        - All files matched by ``path_pattern`` are JSONL compressed with gzip
          (``.jsonl.gz``). Mixed or uncompressed shards are not supported.
        - ``filter_column`` + ``filter_values`` are designed for docid-set filters
          (thousands of values, O(1) set lookup per row). Pass the full qrel docid
          set to guarantee the fidelity rule: every qrels-positive doc is in the
          raw snapshot, so recall is never artificially capped. When both are
          ``None`` the whole dataset streams through; ``max_rows`` caps it.
        - Row counting across shards follows shard alphabetical order. A partial
          last shard is consumed only to the cap — its remaining bytes are not
          downloaded.

    Alternatives rejected:
        - Extending :class:`HuggingFaceDataset` with a ``file_mode`` flag: the
          two loading paths (``load_dataset`` vs ``HfFileSystem + gzip``) import
          entirely different libraries and share zero logic. A flag would produce
          a class with two unrelated personalities. A dedicated class keeps each
          path independently followable.
        - ``hf_hub_download`` per shard (requires enumerating all shard names
          up front): ``HfFileSystem.glob`` lists the directory lazily without
          materialising every path, which is what streaming decompression needs.

    Requires the ``hf`` extra (``uv sync --extra hf``).
    """

    _MUTABLE_REFS = frozenset({"main", "master", "head", "refs/heads/main"})
    _PLACEHOLDER_REF = "replace_with_commit_sha"

    def __init__(
        self,
        repo_id: str,
        revision: str,
        path_pattern: str,
        max_rows: int | None = None,
        filter_column: str | None = None,
        filter_values: list[str] | None = None,
        token_env: str = "HF_TOKEN",
    ) -> None:
        normalized_ref = (revision or "").strip().lower()
        if normalized_ref == self._PLACEHOLDER_REF:
            msg = (
                f"HfFileDataset({repo_id!r}): revision is still the placeholder. "
                f"Resolve the real SHA and paste it into conf/prod/catalog.yml:\n"
                f"  uv run python -c \"from huggingface_hub import HfApi; "
                f"print(HfApi().dataset_info('{repo_id}').sha)\""
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg)
        if not normalized_ref or normalized_ref in self._MUTABLE_REFS:
            msg = (
                f"HfFileDataset({repo_id!r}): revision must pin an immutable "
                f"commit SHA or tag, got {revision!r}."
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg)
        self._repo_id = repo_id
        self._revision = revision
        self._path_pattern = path_pattern
        self._max_rows = max_rows
        self._filter_column = filter_column
        # Convert to a set once so per-row lookup is O(1).
        self._filter_values: frozenset[str] | None = (
            frozenset(filter_values) if filter_values is not None else None
        )
        self._token_env = token_env

    def load(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        import gzip
        import json

# Production catalog overrides: `kedro run --env prod --pipeline production`.
#
# Replaces the NOSIBLE/prediction source with the two real-data sources:
#   CC-News spine   (stanford-oval/ccnews)      — ~192k English articles
#   MIRACL corpus   (miracl/miracl-corpus en)   — ~8k passages (all qrel positives)
# Together they form a ~200k-document, 256-shard index.
#
# Requires the `hf` extra:  uv sync --extra hf --extra st
# Neither dataset is gated: HF_TOKEN is not required.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# 01_raw — acquisition                                                #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

raw_ccnews_source:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.HuggingFaceDataset
  repo_id: stanford-oval/ccnews
  # SHA pinned 2026-08-14 from:
  #   uv run python -c "from huggingface_hub import HfApi; \
  #     print(HfApi().dataset_info('stanford-oval/ccnews').sha)"
  revision: d733e654c9a506df519e1a166a86c118c7657ce4
  split: train
  streaming: true
  # filter_equals is applied before islice so max_rows counts English rows only,
  # not the full multilingual stream. Critical for CC-News which is 100M+ rows
  # across ~90 languages.
  filter_equals:
    language: en
  # 193k rows ≈ 200k target minus the ~7,921 mandatory MIRACL passages, with
  # headroom for rows dropped by the min_text_chars filter in normalize_rows.
  max_rows: 193000

raw_ccnews:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/01_raw/ccnews_miracl_ccnews_snapshot.jsonl

raw_miracl_source:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.HfFileDataset
  repo_id: miracl/miracl-corpus
  # SHA pinned 2026-08-14 from:
  #   uv run python -c "from huggingface_hub import HfApi; \
  #     print(HfApi().dataset_info('miracl/miracl-corpus').sha)"
  revision: d921ec7e349ce0d28daf30b2da9da5ee698bef0d
  # English passages only. Docid-set filtering (to the 7,921 qrel-referenced
  # passages) is applied inside the corpus_ingest node using the loaded qrels,
  # not here — the node receives both sources and can pass filter_values at
  # runtime. The raw snapshot holds only the filtered passages (01_raw principle:
  # never re-download, nodes.py:38).
  path_pattern: "miracl-corpus-v1.0-en/*.jsonl.gz"

raw_miracl:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/01_raw/ccnews_miracl_miracl_snapshot.jsonl

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# 02_intermediate — normalised to the Document schema                 #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

normalized_ccnews:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/02_intermediate/ccnews_miracl_ccnews_documents.jsonl

normalized_miracl:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/02_intermediate/ccnews_miracl_miracl_documents.jsonl

merged_documents:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/02_intermediate/ccnews_miracl_merged_documents.jsonl

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# 03_primary — the build-ready corpus                                 #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

documents:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:input_path,data/03_primary/ccnews_miracl_corpus.jsonl}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# The index                                                           #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

shard_index:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.ShardIndexDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:index_path,artifacts/ccnews-miracl-200k}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# MIRACL en-dev judgment pipeline (task #5 / M1.4)                   #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Run standalone: kedro run --env prod --pipeline judgment_ingest
# Or as part of production (documents must exist first for validation).

miracl_en_dev_source:
  # load_dataset("miracl/miracl") is blocked by a deprecated loading script
  # (miracl.py). MiraclTsvDataset reads the underlying TSV files directly via
  # HfFileSystem and assembles them into the same structured row format.
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.MiraclTsvDataset
  repo_id: miracl/miracl
  # SHA pinned 2026-08-14 from:
  #   uv run python -c "from huggingface_hub import HfApi; \
  #     print(HfApi().dataset_info('miracl/miracl').sha)"
  revision: 5be20db9509754dadad47689368639fcec739c00
  language: en
  split: dev

# Intermediate: unvalidated judgments before the corpus cross-check.
miracl_judgments_unvalidated:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/02_intermediate/miracl_en_dev_judgments_unvalidated.jsonl

# Final validated judgments consumed by the evaluation pipeline.
judgments:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/03_primary/miracl_en_dev_judgments.jsonl

Using the streaming loader (task #3) and qrels loader (task #5): (1) Pull a small REAL fixture slice — all docs referenced by ~25 MIRACL en dev queries (every qrels positive included) plus ~200 CC-News en docs (< 250 CC-News docs total for licensing) — and commit it to data/01_raw/fixtures/ as documents.jsonl + judgments.jsonl in canonical Document/Judgment form, with a small script or documented command showing how it was produced (reproducible: pinned SHAs from .omc/research/m1-discovery.md). (2) Repoint everything that used data/sample: configs/tiny.yaml, Makefile build-sample/search-sample/eval-sample targets → build-fixture/search-fixture/eval-fixture (Makefile:17-32), tests/conftest.py and any test reading data/sample (rg 'data/sample' to find them). Keep the offline hash-provider path working for tests (configs/tiny.yaml stays offline-safe). (3) Write data/ATTRIBUTION.md + data/LICENSE-DATA: CC-News (per-article publisher copyright, Common Crawl ToU, cite stanford-oval/ccnews + SHA), MIRACL (Apache-2.0 + SHA). (4) Delete data/sample/ and scripts/generate_sample_corpus.py; acceptance: `rg -l "data/sample|generate_sample_corpus"` has no hits in src/, tests/, conf/, configs/, Makefile, scripts/. (5) `make test` fully green OFFLINE after the switch (the fixture is the new test substrate). Run `uv run ruff check .` too. This is the M1 done-when task: no fabricated record remains anywhere.

content.subject: M4.2-4.4: calibration + 200k build + eval + baseline doc
content.description: Per Phase 2.2-2.4 of .omc/plans/m1-m4-real-data-eval-baseline.md. All M1 tasks and shard_recall@N (#4) must be complete. (1) Calibration: run the production pipeline with max_rows≈20k (`scripts/with-accel.sh uv run kedro run --env prod --pipeline production --params ...` or a temporary max_rows override — do NOT edit the committed conf for this), record wall-clock; extrapolate to 200k and report the estimate to team-lead BEFORE starting the full run (lead decides go/no-go if extrapolation exceeds ~4h). (2) Full run: 200k docs / 256 shards with `scripts/with-accel.sh` (MPS + thread tuning), then `uv run kedro run --env prod --pipeline evaluation`. Record wall-clock + peak RSS (e.g. /usr/bin/time -l). (3) Verify acceptance criteria 2-4 of the plan: 256 shards present, doc count in [190k, 200k], every judgment docid resolves in the index, eval_report.json has 4 modes × 5 metrics incl. shard_recall@N with no all-zero/NaN mode. (4) Write docs/baselines/ccnews-miracl-200k.md: per-mode metric table, corpus SHAs, embedder revision (conf/prod/parameters.yml), shard count, build wall-clock, machine description; label metrics as MIRACL benchmark metrics never to be merged with generated per-shard evals (scope Amendment #7). (5) Sanity gates: hybrid must not underperform BOTH lexical and dense; shard_recall@N must beat random-N baseline (compute random baseline as N/256 expected). On gate failure: report to team-lead with the numbers, do NOT tune. Commit the baseline doc + eval report.
